entry.title: I made Codedraft proactive!
entry.summary:
CodeDraft is now active and observant. Instead of waiting for you to remember to capture learnings, it works in the background to suggest them at the right time! ⚡️💪🏽
If you are just hearing about Codedraft, it is an intelligent coding extension that helps you turn your daily coding into publishable drafts for blogs or social media. Read more about it here CodeDraft now watches your activity (file saves, git commits) to identify "interesting" moments. How to Verify: Open a source file (TypeScript/JavaScript). Make a significant change (e.g., add a new function with >20 lines or add a try/catch block). Save the file. Result: You should see a notification: "Interesting change detected. Capture this learning?" When you commit code, CodeDraft analyses the message and changes. Here is how you can verify the changes: Stage some changes. Commit with a message containing keywords like fix, refactor, or feat (e.g., git commit -m "fix: resolve null pointer exception"). Result: CodeDraft will prompt: "Significant commit detected: ... Capture this learning?" A new status bar item keeps you informed. 👁️ (Eye Icon): CodeDraft is watching (0 pending captures). Weekly Review: On Fridays at 5 PM (configurable), it reminds you to review your week's learnings. You can customise the proactive behaviour in VS Code settings (CodeDraft > Proactive): Try using CodeDraft for a day of normal work. Quick Links

Contribute: GitHub Repository
Report Issues: GitHub Issues
